paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you've been handed something that lasts, so live like it. Peter says to prepare your minds for action and set your hope fully on the grace to be given at the revelation of Jesus Christ (1 Peter 1:13). He says to be holy in all you do, because it is written: "Be holy, because I am holy." (1 Peter 1:15-16). That's not a rule for show. It's a family resemblance, and you're called by a Father who is holy.

And look at what it cost. You were not redeemed with perishable things such as silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot (1 Peter 1:18-19). Nobody can pay that price back, and that's the point! You live in reverent fear as a foreigner here (1 Peter 1:17), not to earn your place, but because you know what it took to bring you in. I've been forgotten in the dark, and I'm telling you, being found makes you want to do right by the One who found you.

So what does that look like on a Tuesday? Love one another deeply, from a pure heart (1 Peter 1:22). You've been born again through the living and enduring word of God (1 Peter 1:23), and Peter says "the grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of the Lord stands forever." (1 Peter 1:24-25). Everything else fades, baker, even my glorious mustache. Build your life on the One thing that stays.
